entries.title: Acts 27:8
segments:
Fair Havens. A bay on the southern coast of Crete.  It still retains its ancient name.
 

 
Lasea. A city about four miles east of Fair Havens.  It ruins were discovered in 1856.  Neither Fair Havens nor Lasea is known to have been mentioned by any other writer than the writer of Acts.

entries.title: Acts 27:9
segments: The Fast. That was observed on the Day of Atonement, the tenth day of Tishri, the seventh month of the Jewish year, about the same as the latter part of September and the first part of October.  Storms were the to be expected.

entries.title: Acts 27:40
segments: The bands of the rudders. That is, lowering the rudders again into the water so that the ship could be steered safely.  The ships of ancient times had two large oar-shaped rudders, which in this case had been raised out of the water and tied fast while the ship was drifting, so that they might not be destroyed.

entries.title: Acts 27:41
segments: Where two seas meet. A narrow strait between the coast of Malta and the small island of Salmonetta.
